questions.q: How did Jim feel about Treasure Island from his first look at it that morning?
choices: He hated the very thought of it
He was thrilled and could not wait to land
He felt calm and safe
He was bored by the sight of it
questions.evidence: I hated the very thought of Treasure Island

questions.q: What made the Spy-glass hill stand out from the other hills?
choices: It was the tallest and flat on top like a pedestal
It was covered in bright green grass all the way up
It had a thin line of smoke rising from its top
It was the smallest and lowest hill on the island
questions.evidence: cut off at the top like a pedestal to put a statue on

questions.q: Why did the boats have to tow (warp) the ship to the anchorage?
choices: There was no sign of any wind
The ship's rudder had been broken
The sails had been torn in a storm
The captain wanted to save the sails
questions.evidence: there was no sign of any wind

questions.q: Why did Jim think Anderson's grumbling in the boat was a bad sign?
choices: The men had always worked willingly, so discipline was slipping
Anderson was usually the captain's most loyal and cheerful man
It meant the boat was leaking and about to sink
Anderson had never said a word on the whole voyage
questions.evidence: the very sight of the island had relaxed the cords of discipline

questions.q: Who guided the ship through the narrow passage without ever hesitating?
choices: Long John Silver
Captain Smollett
Squire Trelawney
Job Anderson

questions.q: What did Dr. Livesey think the bad smell at the anchorage meant?
choices: There was fever there
The treasure was buried close by
A ship had sunk there
Pirates were cooking on the shore
questions.evidence: I'll stake my wig there's fever here

questions.q: "Mutiny, it was plain, hung over us like a thunder-cloud." What is a mutiny?
choices: A rebellion of sailors against their officers
A long, still spell at sea with no wind at all
A sickness that sailors catch in swamps
A celebration held after reaching land
questions.evidence: Mutiny, it was plain, hung over us like a thunder-cloud.

questions.q: How did Long John Silver behave while the rest of the crew was sulking?
choices: He was all smiles, obeyed cheerfully, and sang songs
He growled and refused orders just like the others
He hid away in the galley all afternoon long
He argued openly with the captain on deck
questions.evidence: he was all smiles to everyone

questions.q: Why did the captain say Silver was the one man they could rely on?
choices: Silver also wanted to keep things quiet and could calm the men
Silver was secretly loyal to the squire and hated all the other pirates
Silver was the only one who knew where the treasure lay
Silver had promised to fight the others if they rose up
questions.evidence: he's as anxious as you and I to smother things up

questions.q: What was the captain's plan to calm the restless crew?
choices: Let the men go ashore for the afternoon
Give every man an extra ration of rum
Lock the ringleaders down in the hold
Sail away from the island at once
questions.evidence: Let's allow the men an afternoon ashore

questions.q: Which three men were told about the danger and given the cabin party's trust?
choices: Hunter, Joyce, and Redruth
Anderson, Silver, and Tom
Israel Hands, Merry, and Morgan
Alan, Dick, and Anderson
questions.evidence: Hunter, Joyce, and Redruth were taken into our confidence

questions.q: What happened right after the crew was split up, with six men staying on board?
choices: Jim slipped over the side into one of the boats going ashore
The captain fired a gun to call the men back to the ship at once
Silver locked the cabin door from the outside
The ship began to sail back out to the open sea
questions.evidence: In a jiffy I had slipped over the side and curled up in the fore-sheets of the nearest boat

questions.q: When did Jim first begin to regret going ashore?
choices: When Silver called out to ask if it was him
When he saw a snake coiled on the rocks
When the boat almost tipped over in the surf
When the captain fired the ship's gun
questions.evidence: from that moment I began to regret what I had done

questions.q: What is this chapter mostly about?
choices: The crew nears mutiny and Jim sneaks ashore with Silver's men
Jim finds the treasure buried under a tall tree on the hill
The ship is wrecked in a storm near the island and sinks
The captain and Silver become good friends and trust each other
questions.evidence: It occurred to me at once to go ashore.
